gloss: to think up; to hit upon; to come up with

definitions.gloss: to think up; to hit upon; to come up with
definitions.explanation: To arrive at an idea or solution through thought. Emphasizes reaching the idea by thinking rather than its merely occurring to one.

examples.japanese: いい{方法|ほうほう}を{考|かんが}え{付|つ}いた。
examples.english: I thought of a good method.

examples.japanese: {誰|だれ}もそんな{計画|けいかく}は{考|かんが}え{付|つ}かなかった。
examples.english: No one came up with such a plan.

examples.japanese: {問題|もんだい}の{解決策|かいけつさく}をなかなか{考|かんが}え{付|つ}くことができなかった。
examples.english: I couldn't manage to come up with a solution to the problem.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: Transitive godan verb. Xを{考|かんが}え{付|つ}く. Compound of {考|かんが}える (to think) + {付|つ}く (to occur to). Emphasizes reaching an idea through active thought.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {方法|ほうほう}を{考|かんが}え{付|つ}く: to think up a method
- いい{案|あん}を{考|かんが}え{付|つ}く: to come up with a good idea

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {思|おも}い{付|つ}く: to hit upon — the idea simply occurs to one, with less emphasis on deliberate thinking
- {考|かんが}え{出|だ}す: to think out — similar, with a slightly stronger sense of producing the idea
